AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: This work aims to investigate the impact of gestational age and fetal gender on fetal heart rate (FHR) tracings.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Different linear and non-linear parameters indicating correlation or complexity were used to study the influence of fetal age and gender on FHR tracings. The signals were recorded from 99 normal pregnant women in a singleton pregnancy at gestational age from 28 to 40 weeks, before the onset of labor. 56 of the fetuses were female and 43 were male.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The analysis of FHR has shown that mean as well as measures of irregularity of FHR, such as approximate entropy and algorithmic complexity, decrease as gestation progresses. There was also indicated that Mutual information and Multiscale Entropy were lower in male fetuses in early pregnancy.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Fetal age and gender seem to influence FHR tracings. Taking this into consideration would improve the interpretation of FHR monitoring.
